items.title: A cultural park, seen from above
items.alt: Change the viewpoint. Streets establish scale; tower terraces suggest height; seating and paths connect the theatre, pavilion and garden.
items.explanation: Change the viewpoint. Streets establish scale; tower terraces suggest height; seating and paths connect the theatre, pavilion and garden.

items.title: Beneath the surface
items.alt: Change material and context. Reflected light, circular forms, fish, kelp and the seabed suggest an underwater world without prescribing one story.
items.explanation: Change material and context. Reflected light, circular forms, fish, kelp and the seabed suggest an underwater world without prescribing one story.

items.title: In the middle of making
items.alt: Combine objects with traces. A cup, coffee reflections, shadows, wet residue and drawing materials suggest an inhabited desk and leave its story open.
items.explanation: Combine objects with traces. A cup, coffee reflections, shadows, wet residue and drawing materials suggest an inhabited desk and leave its story open.

items.title: A route through the canyon
items.alt: Terraced rock edges, tiny houses, roads and approaching walkers turn the gap into a traversable landscape.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Change scale Convincing clues: Terraced rock edges, tiny houses, roads and approaching walkers turn the gap into a traversable landscape.
details: Thinking shift: Change scale
Convincing clues: Terraced rock edges, tiny houses, roads and approaching walkers turn the gap into a traversable landscape.

items.title: The light nobody drew
items.alt: A light source, curtain folds, a stool, microphone and audience make untouched paper read as illumination.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Change physical meaning Convincing clues: A light source, curtain folds, a stool, microphone and audience make untouched paper read as illumination.
details: Thinking shift: Change physical meaning
Convincing clues: A light source, curtain folds, a stool, microphone and audience make untouched paper read as illumination.

items.title: Someone was here
items.alt: A damaged print, conservatory plants and two surviving hands turn the missing middle into an open story.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Infer causes from absence Convincing clues: A damaged print, conservatory plants and two surviving hands turn the missing middle into an open story.
details: Thinking shift: Infer causes from absence
Convincing clues: A damaged print, conservatory plants and two surviving hands turn the missing middle into an open story.

items.title: A drop with a whole world inside
items.alt: A glass slide, translucent organisms, internal structures and a microscope scale bar suggest microscopic pond life. This is an illustration, not a biological identification.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Shrink the observer Convincing clues: A glass slide, translucent organisms, internal structures and a microscope scale bar suggest microscopic pond life. This is an illustration, not a biological identification.
details: First assumption: The large circle is an everyday object.
Thinking shift: Shrink the observer
Convincing clues: A glass slide, translucent organisms, internal structures and a microscope scale bar suggest microscopic pond life. This is an illustration, not a biological identification.
Another direction: Try a cross-section of a fruit rather than pond water.

items.title: An island park from above
items.alt: Trees, footbridges, tiny people, buildings and boats establish a large circular lake with islands.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Turn marks into a mapped landscape Convincing clues: Trees, footbridges, tiny people, buildings and boats establish a large circular lake with islands.
details: First assumption: The small circles are details on an object.
Thinking shift: Turn marks into a mapped landscape
Convincing clues: Trees, footbridges, tiny people, buildings and boats establish a large circular lake with islands.
Another direction: Make a crater research station or a flood-control basin.

items.title: A quiet shift above the clouds
items.alt: Bolted framing, handrails, control panels and a tethered mug make the outer circle a human-sized window; distant worlds lie beyond it.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Separate frame scale from subject distance Convincing clues: Bolted framing, handrails, control panels and a tethered mug make the outer circle a human-sized window; distant worlds lie beyond it.
details: First assumption: The outer circle contains the three smaller objects.
Thinking shift: Separate frame scale from subject distance
Convincing clues: Bolted framing, handrails, control panels and a tethered mug make the outer circle a human-sized window; distant worlds lie beyond it.
Another direction: Use a diving-bell window with fish at different distances.

items.title: The visitor that left a silver path
items.alt: A spiral shell, antennae, wet leaves and a silvery trail suggest a snail that has already crossed the paving.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Read a line as a leftover trace Convincing clues: A spiral shell, antennae, wet leaves and a silvery trail suggest a snail that has already crossed the paving.
details: First assumption: The broken line is a route drawn on a map.
Thinking shift: Read a line as a leftover trace
Convincing clues: A spiral shell, antennae, wet leaves and a silvery trail suggest a snail that has already crossed the paving.
Another direction: Try tyre marks, a dragged toy or ripples behind a duck.

items.title: A warm drink in a cooling room
items.alt: A saucer, handle and coffee surface establish a stationary cup. Vapour fragments rise away from it, suggesting cooling over time.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Let the object stay and something escape Convincing clues: A saucer, handle and coffee surface establish a stationary cup. Vapour fragments rise away from it, suggesting cooling over time.
details: First assumption: The circle must have travelled along the line.
Thinking shift: Let the object stay and something escape
Convincing clues: A saucer, handle and coffee surface establish a stationary cup. Vapour fragments rise away from it, suggesting cooling over time.
Another direction: Try scent leaving a flower or sparks from a forge.

items.title: The wall just before it gives way
items.alt: A crane cable, suspended ball, cracked brick wall and rubble turn the dashed arc into a motion cue and invite the next frame.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Use motion to anticipate the next moment Convincing clues: A crane cable, suspended ball, cracked brick wall and rubble turn the dashed arc into a motion cue and invite the next frame.
details: First assumption: The marks describe something that already happened.
Thinking shift: Use motion to anticipate the next moment
Convincing clues: A crane cable, suspended ball, cracked brick wall and rubble turn the dashed arc into a motion cue and invite the next frame.
Another direction: Try a pendulum clock, playground swing or a ball approaching a window.

items.title: Two rooftops, one shared garden
items.alt: Building floors establish rooftops. A railed bridge, people, planters and tables turn them into a shared place.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Connect places through shared use Convincing clues: Building floors establish rooftops. A railed bridge, people, planters and tables turn them into a shared place.
details: First assumption: The squares are separate, self-contained objects.
Thinking shift: Connect places through shared use
Convincing clues: Building floors establish rooftops. A railed bridge, people, planters and tables turn them into a shared place.
Another direction: Make the squares two riverbanks linked by a ferry.

items.title: A conversation across two rooms
items.alt: Two desks, headsets, screens with complementary puzzle pieces and two-way arrows suggest collaboration across rooms. The arrows are diagrammatic exchange cues.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Make the pair complementary Convincing clues: Two desks, headsets, screens with complementary puzzle pieces and two-way arrows suggest collaboration across rooms. The arrows are diagrammatic exchange cues.
details: First assumption: Similar squares must show the same thing.
Thinking shift: Make the pair complementary
Convincing clues: Two desks, headsets, screens with complementary puzzle pieces and two-way arrows suggest collaboration across rooms. The arrows are diagrammatic exchange cues.
Another direction: Try a sender and receiver, kitchen and dining room, or two musicians answering each other.

items.title: A window and a way of seeing
items.alt: One frame is a divided window onto mountains. The other is an easel-mounted painting with related colours and simplified forms; brushes and a palette establish interpretation.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Turn one into a representation of the other Convincing clues: One frame is a divided window onto mountains. The other is an easel-mounted painting with related colours and simplified forms; brushes and a palette establish interpretation.
details: First assumption: Both squares are objects of the same kind.
Thinking shift: Turn one into a representation of the other
Convincing clues: One frame is a divided window onto mountains. The other is an easel-mounted painting with related colours and simplified forms; brushes and a palette establish interpretation.
Another direction: Try a real garden beside its map, or a building beside its blueprint.

items.title: Soft folds
items.alt: A rail, hanging rings and a stitched hem turn curves into folds.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Same curves, different material. Convincing clues: A rail, hanging rings and a stitched hem turn curves into folds.
details: Thinking shift: Same curves, different material.
Convincing clues: A rail, hanging rings and a stitched hem turn curves into folds.
What remains if you remove the stitching?

items.title: A surface that moves
items.alt: Banks, a boat, ripples and a wake suggest flowing water.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Same curves, different material. Convincing clues: Banks, a boat, ripples and a wake suggest flowing water.
details: Thinking shift: Same curves, different material.
Convincing clues: Banks, a boat, ripples and a wake suggest flowing water.
Would colour alone convince you?

items.title: Grain with a history
items.alt: A cut surface, growth rings, a knot and roots suggest wood.
items.explanation: Thinking shift: Same curves, different material. Convincing clues: A cut surface, growth rings, a knot and roots suggest wood.
details: Thinking shift: Same curves, different material.
Convincing clues: A cut surface, growth rings, a knot and roots suggest wood.
Which clue still works if you change the colour?

items.title: A cat beneath the table
items.alt: From floor level, a window frames a bird. The two short starter lines form the upper edges of two stacked books; table legs and cat ears frame the view.
items.explanation: Lower the observer to cat height. Table legs hide part of the room, while the bird outside becomes the centre of attention.
details: Thinking shift: Lower the observer to cat height. Table legs hide part of the room, while the bird outside becomes the centre of attention.
Reflect: Where is your observer, and what can they see that someone else cannot?

items.title: Looking out from underwater
items.alt: A submerged observer sees a rectangular viewing window with fish beyond it. The two starter lines become the tops of ladder rungs, with rails extending down through bubbles.
items.explanation: Put the observer underwater. Bubbles and fish establish the medium; the ladder suggests a route to the surface.
details: Thinking shift: Put the observer underwater. Bubbles and fish establish the medium; the ladder suggests a route to the surface.
Reflect: Where is your observer, and what can they see that someone else cannot?

items.title: A small robot approaches a charging dock
items.alt: A robot camera view frames a rectangular charging panel. The two starter lines become charging contacts below it. Floor perspective lines lead towards the dock; battery and scan indicators frame the view.
items.explanation: Use a machine as the observer. A battery indicator and alignment guides make the same room a navigation task.
details: Thinking shift: Use a machine as the observer. A battery indicator and alignment guides make the same room a navigation task.
Reflect: Where is your observer, and what can they see that someone else cannot?

items.title: A tiny rain gauge
items.alt: An upright spoon catches falling raindrops. Measuring marks cross its bowl, and its handle is planted in a flower bed beside small seedlings.
items.explanation: A hollow bowl can collect rain. The planted handle anchors it, while level marks turn a utensil into a measuring instrument.
details: Thinking shift: A hollow bowl can collect rain. The planted handle anchors it, while level marks turn a utensil into a measuring instrument.
Reflect: Which property of the spoon makes its new job possible?

items.title: A reflector for a lost traveller
items.alt: Sun rays strike the spoon bowl and reflect towards a distant rescue boat. A hand holds the long handle; hills and a waterline establish the outdoor setting.
items.explanation: A shiny surface can redirect light. Rays, a holding hand and a distant boat suggest signalling instead of eating.
details: Thinking shift: A shiny surface can redirect light. Rays, a holding hand and a distant boat suggest signalling instead of eating.
Reflect: Which property of the spoon makes its new job possible?

items.title: A wind chime striker
items.alt: A spoon hangs from a string between two suspended hollow tubes. Curved motion marks indicate that its bowl swings against the tubes; a breeze moves leaves nearby.
items.explanation: A hard surface can make sound. Suspension, nearby tubes and motion marks suggest a wind chime striker.
details: Thinking shift: A hard surface can make sound. Suspension, nearby tubes and motion marks suggest a wind chime striker.
Reflect: Which property of the spoon makes its new job possible?

items.title: Three empty places in a museum
items.alt: Three incomplete outlines sit on a museum display wall above empty label plates. A spotlight, a fallen hanging cord and a trail of footprints suggest that exhibits have been removed. No missing exhibit is drawn.
items.explanation: Absence can tell a story. Empty labels and footprints suggest removal, but do not prove whether this was a theft, a loan or a new exhibition.
details: Thinking shift: Absence can tell a story. Empty labels and footprints suggest removal, but do not prove whether this was a theft, a loan or a new exhibition.
Reflect: Which clue suggests the missing thing? Could another explanation fit?

items.title: The tools have gone
items.alt: Three incomplete outlines are surrounded by pegs on a workshop board. An open toolbox and dusty marks below the board suggest that objects once stored here are elsewhere. The gaps remain blank.
items.explanation: A storage outline is evidence of an absent object. Pegs and an open toolbox suggest use or relocation without showing the missing tools.
details: Thinking shift: A storage outline is evidence of an absent object. Pegs and an open toolbox suggest use or relocation without showing the missing tools.
Reflect: Which clue suggests the missing thing? Could another explanation fit?

items.title: Traces at a dig
items.alt: The three incomplete outlines lie within a marked excavation grid. A brush, numbered marker flags and scattered grains surround them; the missing parts are not filled in.
items.explanation: Treat the outlines as traces in the ground. Survey markers and a brush invite reconstruction, while several explanations remain possible.
details: Thinking shift: Treat the outlines as traces in the ground. Survey markers and a brush invite reconstruction, while several explanations remain possible.
Reflect: Which clue suggests the missing thing? Could another explanation fit?

items.title: Welcome / Keep out
items.alt: Two panels repeat the same circle, tall rectangle and short line. In the left panel a smiling face, door handle, flowers and welcome mat invite entry. In the right, an angry face, door bars and warning sign discourage entry.
items.explanation: The unchanged shapes become a face, a door and a mat. Expression and access cues reverse the invitation.
details: Thinking shift: The unchanged shapes become a face, a door and a mat. Expression and access cues reverse the invitation.
Reflect: Which added detail changes the interpretation most? What stays the same?

items.title: Shelter / Obstruction
items.alt: The same circle becomes the sun and the same rectangle a wall in two panels. On the left a seated person rests in the wall’s shaded area. On the right a walking person faces the wall blocking the route to a flag.
items.explanation: The wall can protect or obstruct. Heat and a resting figure make shade helpful; a destination beyond the wall makes it a barrier.
details: Thinking shift: The wall can protect or obstruct. Heat and a resting figure make shade helpful; a destination beyond the wall makes it a barrier.
Reflect: Which added detail changes the interpretation most? What stays the same?

items.title: A welcome rain / A ruined picnic
items.alt: The same circle, rectangle and short line repeat in two scenes. Rain, seedlings and a water tank suggest relief for a dry garden on the left. Rain, a wet picnic table and a person seeking cover suggest disrupted plans on the right.
items.explanation: The weather is identical, but the goal changes. Rain helps the garden and spoils an outdoor meal; both readings can be true.
details: Thinking shift: The weather is identical, but the goal changes. Rain helps the garden and spoils an outdoor meal; both readings can be true.
Reflect: Which added detail changes the interpretation most? What stays the same?

items.title: Windows with a view
items.alt: Three green arches become tall windows in a warm stone wall, with crossing window bars and planted window boxes.
items.explanation: Vertical sides, crossbars and window boxes make the arches read as windows.
details: Thinking shift: Vertical sides, crossbars and window boxes make the arches read as windows.
Reflect: What other role could these arches play?

items.title: A tiny forest
items.alt: Three green arches become mushroom caps above slender stems, with spots, gills and grass.
items.explanation: A flat cap edge, stem and small spots make the arches read as mushrooms.
details: Thinking shift: A flat cap edge, stem and small spots make the arches read as mushrooms.
Reflect: What other role could these arches play?

items.title: A way across
items.alt: Three green arches form bridge openings below a continuous walkway and railing, with water ripples below and a person above.
items.explanation: A shared walkway, supporting piers and water connect the arches into a bridge.
details: Thinking shift: A shared walkway, supporting piers and water connect the arches into a bridge.
Reflect: What other role could these arches play?
